title: Aleatoric vs Epistemic Uncertainty
interviewAnswer: Aleatoric uncertainty comes from irreducible data noise; epistemic uncertainty comes from limited model knowledge and can often be reduced with better data.
why: Production systems often need to know when a prediction is uncertain and why.
intuition: A noisy sensor can remain ambiguous with infinite data; a model seeing a new population is uncertain because it lacks knowledge.
deepDive: The decomposition is model-dependent. Heteroscedastic likelihoods can model aleatoric noise; ensembles/Bayesian methods can approximate epistemic uncertainty.
commonMistakes: Equating softmax confidence with epistemic uncertainty.
Claiming all uncertainty disappears with more data.
production: Use uncertainty to trigger abstention, human review or safe fallback.
workedExample: A medical model may be uncertain because the scan itself is ambiguous or because the patient population differs from training.
